page: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz on an arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor, allocating a single dedicated thread per core without hyperthreading. The processor integrates 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without integrated local storage, and includes no GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation highlights competitive multi-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench multi-core workloads, the system attains a top-tier score of 25,571.0, accompanied by a Clang software compilation score of 81,934.0 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 109,145.77. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 652.5 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations register at 46,812.99. Redis throughput reaches 131.06 million SET operations per second alongside 120.85 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 459.06 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 196.93 GB/sec for large-block writes. Conversely, single-thread performance reflects mid-tier outcomes, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,892.0 and single-core stress-ng throughput of 1,706.7.

From an architectural standpoint, the dedicated physical core distribution and elevated memory throughput deliver strong resource efficiency for concurrent processing tasks. However, users relying on large in-memory footprints must consider the 2.0 GB per core threshold. Additionally, all persistent data requires attached network storage due to the absence of bundled local NVMe drives.

Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is aligned with parallelized compute workloads, such as software compilation pipelines, distributed caching systems, batch processing, video encoding, microservices clusters, and medium-scale web application infrastructure.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon at 2.8 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 128.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core performance, achieving 25,571.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing, 81,934.0 in Clang software compilation, and 131.06 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, driven by 459.06 GB/sec large-block uncached read memory bandwidth. Single-core throughput remains mid-tier, shown by a 1,892.0 Geekbench single-core score. Due to its dedicated core execution profile, high network throughput, and low memory-to-core ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, software compilation farms, web servers, and distributed caching clusters.
